children: The Brazilian government has allocated an additional 6.6 billion reais ($1.3 billion) for fuel subsidies, according to an executive order signed by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Wednesday, when a subsidy for gasoline was set to expire.
The order provides some 5.6 billion reais to subsidize diesel for road use and the remaining 998 million reais is to subsidize the production and import of oil-based fuels.
Lula's administration has crafted a series of measures for the fuel sector, as a part of a broad relief plan established since the start of the
The leftist leader is seeking to cushion the impact of higher global oil prices on domestic consumers ahead of an October election, when he will seek another four-year term.

A previous subsidy on gasoline, extended in August, is set to expire on Wednesday. In June, the government decided to eliminate part of a diesel subsidy when oil prices retreated, but the external relief proved temporary and the conflict is ongoing.

Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel on Wednesday for the first time since July 24, hitting a six-week high as the escalation in the Middle East raised concerns over disruptions to global oil supplies.
